about: The words RecipeTextSplitter reads free text with: a Reddit post (#11) or the lines read from a photo (#198), in the text's own detected language (#208). Headers are compared lowercased, without what may surround them (a symbol, a trailing colon, a parenthetical). ingredientHeaders, instructionHeaders, endHeaders: whole lines. keywords: one word that ends a header set apart as one (bold, a heading, a colon, capitals) of 2 to 4 words ('Dry ingredients'), or, where keywordFirst, starts it ('Ingredientes secos'); the other words, unless all plainWords, name a group. verbs: a line whose other words hold one is a step, never a header. misspelt: one-word headers two letters off. forHeader: '<keyword> <joiner> ...:' with its colon ('Ingredients for the cake:'), or '<keyword> <joiner> 4 <serving word>' (yield.json's serving words) without. editWords, stepLabels, yield, times, approx, amountUnits, amountPatterns, gluedUnits: case-insensitive regex fragments; editWords and yield words must end in an ASCII letter (a \b follows them). yield.whole keeps the line ('Serves 4'), yield.labels are dropped ('Servings: 4'), yield.for keeps '<for> 4 <serving word>' whole. amountUnits: a number before one makes a line an amount ('Salt – 1/2 tsp'); amountPatterns: other shapes that do. gluedUnits: unit words the scaler reads (units.json) long and distinct enough to flag when run into the next word ('1 cupraisins', PhotoTextSorter.suspect); a short one that starts ordinary words ('g', 'can') is left out, and gluedExceptions are ordinary words that start with one. Empty for a language written without spaces.
